A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same harmonic-decomposition framework for learning single-index models. The main text, both tables, equations, and Appendices A–I are available and can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical algorithms, complexity bounds, and proofs. Tables 1–2 summarize analytical rates; neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical. Its revised mathematical statements and expanded literature discussion introduce no original experimental, simulation, or empirical data-analysis results.

M1.justification: The spectral estimators, online SGD procedure, and balanced and unbalanced harmonic tensor-unfolding algorithms are unchanged, including their transformations and recovery procedures in Appendices D–F.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or evaluation benchmarks. The theoretical spherical and Gaussian single-index settings, including normalized inputs, are retained.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. The added discussions of AMP, spectral methods, and other algorithms are literature positioning, not new evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures are introduced or revised. Changes to analytical sample-complexity bounds are theoretical changes.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies are added or removed. The analytical comparisons concerning radial information and harmonic components, including Appendix A, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Revised detection-hardness statements concern theoretical guarantees, not statistical reporting of measured results.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version, and the analytical rate summaries in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. The revised formal lower bound is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1(ii) weakens the stated lower bound from Omega_d(M*) to Omega_d(M* log(d)^(-Cp)). Appendix C.2 corrects weak detection to advantage over random guessing and specifies strong detection through vanishing type I and II errors. Appendix F.3 corrects a tensor argument, and F.5 restores a beta_d,l factor in the operator-norm bounds, including Eq. (106). These are localized corrections; the main proof framework remains intact.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain unchanged, but the introduction qualifies sample optimality by additional sample–runtime tradeoffs. Equation (3) also changes the Gaussian runtime summary from Theta_d to tilde-Theta_d, narrowing the claimed precision of optimality.

C2.justification: New Remark 3.2 explicitly limits the optimality discussion to matching the exponent in d and leaves finer sample–runtime tradeoffs outside scope. Remark 5.1 qualifies the normalized-input sample requirement as 'at least' d^(k*-1), replacing the previous unqualified rate.

D1.justification: Implementation procedures in Appendices D–F are retained. No code or data access information, hardware specifications, implementation hyperparameters, or measured execution times are added or revised.

R1.justification: New Section 1.2 substantially expands positioning across AMP and spectral thresholds, robust learning, multi-index models, gradient learning, and tensor PCA. It explicitly relates the proposed unfolding estimator to concurrent work by Damian, Lee, and Bruna [DLB25], distinguishing Hermite from harmonic tensors. This extends well beyond v1's scattered comparisons.

P1.justification: V2 adds a related-work subsection and Remark 3.2, expands the normalization calculation in Appendix B.3, and makes localized wording and cross-reference edits. Most prose and the overall section and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their structure, captions, and entries, with no new figures. Appendix B.3 expands a short equation display into a multiline calculation; the contents page and local spacing and page breaks also change.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision through the qualified lower bound in Theorem 1(ii), corrected detection language in Appendix C.2, and restored signal dependence in Appendix F.5. Section 1.2 also provides substantially clearer attribution and comparison with concurrent work. These changes improve reliability and context, while the methods and principal polynomial-rate conclusions remain stable, supporting a limited overall improvement.
